1.q: the house of Judah and Benjamin
1.note: Here “house” is a metonym that represents a tribe or descendants and refers specifically to the soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. Alternate translation: [all the soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin]
“one hundred and eighty thousand chosen men”
“choice men who were soldiers.” The phrase “chosen men” is an idiom that refers to elite soldiers who were skilled in battle. Alternate translation: [of the best soldiers]

2.q: the word of Yahweh came … saying
2.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message … and he said] or [Yahweh spoke these words … and he said]
This is the name of a man.
The expression “man of God” is a respectful way of referring to a prophet of Yahweh. Alternate translation: [the man who belongs to God] or [the prophet of God]

3.q: all Israel in Judah and Benjamin
3.note: Here the word “Israel” refers to the Israelite people who live in the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. Alternate translation: [all of the Israelites in the tribes of Judah and Benjamin]

4.note: This is a reference to the ten northern tribes. By calling them “brothers,” Yahweh emphasizes the family relationship between all of the tribes.

5.q: Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built cities
5.note: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people helped Rehoboam build these cities. Alternate translation: [Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and had his workers build cities]

6.note: These are the names of cities.

10.note: These are the names of cities.

11.note: Here the word “fortresses” refers to fortified cities. That Rehoboam “fortified the fortresses” means that he built up and strengthened the defenses of these fortified cities. Alternate translation: [He strengthened the defenses of the fortified cities]

12.note: Alternate translation: [made the cities very strong]

12.q: Judah and Benjamin belonged to him
12.note: Rehoboam was in control of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.

13.q: The priests and the Levites … went over to him from within their borders
13.note: This could mean: (1) “The priests and Levites … supported Rehoboam from within their borders” or (2) “The priests and Levites … traveled from within their borders to join Rehoboam.”

14.q: Jeroboam and his sons had driven them away
14.note: To “drive away” is an idiom that means to forcefully cause someone to leave. Alternate translation: [Jeroboam and his sons had forced them to leave]

15.q: the goat and calf idols he had made
15.note: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people helped Jeroboam make these idols. Alternate translation: [the goat idols and calf idols that he had his craftsmen make]

16.note: Alternate translation: [People … followed the Levites] or [People … came to Jerusalem after the Levites]

16.q: those who set their hearts to seek Yahweh
16.note: Here the word “hearts” represents the thoughts and desires. The idiom “set their hearts” means to determine to do something. Alternate translation: [those who had determined to seek Yahweh] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))
Worshiping Yahweh is spoken of as if the person were seeking Yahweh. Alternate translation: [to worship Yahweh]

17.q: made Rehoboam son of Solomon strong
17.note: The people supporting Rehoboam as king is spoken of as if they made Rehoboam strong. Alternate translation: [supported Rehoboam son of Solomon as king]

17.q: they walked for three years in the way of David and Solomon
17.note: Here a person’s actions and lifestyle are spoken of as if the person were walking along a path. Alternate translation: [they followed the example of David and Solomon for three years]

18.note: These are the names of women.
These are the names of men.

19.note: These are the names of men.

20.note: These are the names of women.
This idiom means that he married her. Alternate translation: [Rehoboam married Maacah]
These are the names of men.

21.q: eighteen wives and sixty concubines … twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters
21.note: “18 wives and 60 concubines … 28 sons and 60 daughters”

22.q: he had the thought of making him king
22.note: Alternate translation: [he had thought of making Abijah king]

23.q: he scattered all his sons throughout all the land of Judah and Benjamin to every fortified city
23.note: Alternate translation: [he sent all his sons throughout all the land to every fortified city of Judah and Benjamin]
